title: Apex SAT Cognitive Trap Taxonomy
description: Single source of truth for distractor trap identifiers. Every generated distractor MUST carry one of these IDs. IDs are append-only and never renamed once shipped: the Student Model, the error log, and the clone engine all join on them.

traps.label: Premature Calculation Stop
traps.description: Student solves correctly for an intermediate quantity and stops, answering with that quantity instead of the one asked for.
traps.distractor_recipe: Make the intermediate value an available option. Typical: question asks for x+3, 2x, or the value of a second variable; the distractor is x.
traps.tell: Arithmetic is clean; the final translation step is missing.
traps.remediation_cue: Re-read the last clause of the question stem before selecting.

traps.label: Sign Error on Transposition
traps.description: A term changes sign incorrectly when moved across the equals sign, distributed, or factored out.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer the correct magnitude with the opposite sign.
traps.tell: Answer is the exact negative of the correct value.
traps.remediation_cue: Distribute the negative explicitly instead of mentally.

traps.label: Unit or Scale Mismatch
traps.description: Student computes in the given units but the question asks for different units, or ignores a per-unit conversion.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer the value in the unconverted unit (minutes vs hours, cm vs m, per-item vs per-dozen).
traps.tell: Answer differs from correct by a clean conversion factor.
traps.remediation_cue: Circle the unit in the question before computing.

traps.label: Extraneous or Discarded Root
traps.description: Student accepts a root that fails the original equation, or reports one root when both are valid (or vice versa).
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer the extraneous solution, or the sum of both roots when only one is valid.
traps.tell: Answer satisfies the squared/cleared form but not the original.
traps.remediation_cue: Substitute the candidate back into the original equation.

traps.label: Domain or Context Constraint Ignored
traps.description: Student produces a mathematically valid answer that the real-world context forbids (negative count, fractional person, time before start).
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer the context-invalid root as a plausible option.
traps.tell: Answer is negative or non-integer in a counting context.
traps.remediation_cue: Ask what the variable physically represents.

traps.label: Percent Base Swap
traps.description: Percent change computed against the wrong base, or successive percent changes summed instead of compounded.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer the value obtained by using the new value as the base, or by adding the two percentages.
traps.tell: Answer is close to correct but consistently off in one direction.
traps.remediation_cue: Name the base out loud: 'percent of what?'

traps.label: Inverted Ratio or Rate
traps.description: Ratio set up upside down; rate multiplied where it should be divided.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer the reciprocal-derived value.
traps.tell: Answer is the reciprocal relationship applied to the same numbers.
traps.remediation_cue: Write the rate with units attached and cancel them.

traps.label: Graph or Table Misread
traps.description: Axis scale, gridline value, intercept, or table header misread.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer the value that results from assuming each gridline is 1, or from swapping the axes.
traps.tell: Answer maps to a real feature of the graph, just the wrong one.
traps.remediation_cue: State the value of one gridline before reading any point.

traps.label: Equation Form Misinterpreted
traps.description: Reads a parameter from the wrong form — treats vertex-form h as a y-value, slope-intercept b as a slope, factored-form root as an intercept of the wrong axis.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer the parameter as read from the wrong slot.
traps.tell: Answer is a number that literally appears in the given equation.
traps.remediation_cue: Name the form before extracting anything from it.

traps.label: Answer Format Violation
traps.description: Correct value, unenterable or misformatted response (percent sign, mixed number, wrong rounding, exceeded character limit).
traps.distractor_recipe: SPR only — tracked as a response-level trap, not an option-level one.
traps.tell: Response is mathematically right and mechanically rejected.
traps.remediation_cue: Convert to decimal or improper fraction before entering.

traps.label: Arithmetic Slip
traps.description: Method correct, computation wrong. The residual category.
traps.distractor_recipe: Use sparingly — at most one option per item, and only with a specific plausible slip modelled.
traps.tell: No conceptual pattern; does not recur on the same skill.
traps.remediation_cue: Verify on Desmos rather than re-checking by hand.

traps.label: Boundary Punctuation — Comma Splice
traps.description: Joins two independent clauses with a comma (or with a comma plus a conjunctive adverb such as 'however').
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer the spliced version alongside the correctly punctuated one; vary only the boundary mark.
traps.tell: Both clauses stand alone as sentences.
traps.remediation_cue: Cover each side of the mark and ask whether it is a complete sentence.

traps.label: Boundary Punctuation — Fused Sentence
traps.description: Runs two independent clauses together with no punctuation at all.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer the unpunctuated join alongside the correctly punctuated one, in a sentence whose clauses read smoothly aloud so the boundary is easy to miss.
traps.tell: Both sides of the join stand alone as sentences and nothing separates them.
traps.remediation_cue: Cover each side of the join and ask whether it is a complete sentence.

traps.label: Improper Subordination at a Boundary
traps.description: Attaches a subordinator or relative pronoun to a clause that must stay independent, producing a fragment or an orphaned relative clause.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer a version that opens the second independent clause with 'which', 'because', or 'although' where no subordination is licensed.
traps.tell: The sentence no longer has a main clause, or the relative pronoun has no sensible antecedent.
traps.remediation_cue: Find the main verb of the whole sentence; if every clause is subordinated, it is a fragment.

traps.label: Unpaired Supplement Punctuation
traps.description: Non-essential element opened with one mark and closed with another (comma…dash), or closed not at all.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer mismatched pairs that read naturally aloud.
traps.tell: Removing the supplement leaves a stray mark.
traps.remediation_cue: Delete the supplement and check the sentence still works.

traps.label: Subject–Verb Agreement Across Distance
traps.description: Verb agrees with an intervening noun rather than the true subject.
traps.distractor_recipe: Place a prepositional phrase with an opposite-number noun between subject and verb.
traps.tell: The wrong verb agrees with the nearest noun.
traps.remediation_cue: Strike out every prepositional phrase, then read subject and verb adjacent.

traps.label: Dangling or Misplaced Modifier
traps.description: Introductory modifier attaches to the wrong noun.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer a version whose subject is the logical actor's possession rather than the actor.
traps.tell: The sentence is grammatical but describes an impossible actor.
traps.remediation_cue: Ask who or what performed the opening phrase.

traps.label: Transition Logical Direction
traps.description: Selects a contrast transition where the logic continues, or a causal one where the relation is merely sequential.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer one transition from each logical family (contrast, continuation, cause, example) so only relation-reading resolves it.
traps.tell: Choice is idiomatic in isolation but reverses the paragraph's logic.
traps.remediation_cue: Summarise both sentences in four words each, then name the relation.

traps.label: Outside Knowledge Import
traps.description: Chooses an option that is true in the world but unsupported by the text.
traps.distractor_recipe: Craft a factually reasonable statement the passage never licenses.
traps.tell: Student cannot point to a line supporting the choice.
traps.remediation_cue: Underline the words in the text that force the answer.

traps.label: Scope Too Broad or Too Narrow
traps.description: Selects a detail as the main idea, or a sweeping generalisation the text supports only locally.
traps.distractor_recipe: Pair one true-but-minor detail with one over-generalised claim.
traps.tell: Choice is accurate about one sentence and wrong about the passage.
traps.remediation_cue: Ask whether the option covers the whole text or one line.

traps.label: Unsupported Absolute
traps.description: Selects an option whose hedging is stronger than the text's ('proves', 'always', 'never', 'the only').
traps.distractor_recipe: Take a correct claim and strengthen one qualifier.
traps.tell: Difference between correct and chosen is a single modal word.
traps.remediation_cue: Circle the qualifier in every option before choosing.

traps.label: Half-Right Option
traps.description: Option's first clause matches the text and its second clause does not; student stops reading at the match.
traps.distractor_recipe: Build a two-clause option with a correct opening and a wrong completion.
traps.tell: Student can defend the first half of the choice only.
traps.remediation_cue: Evaluate every clause of an option, not the first.

traps.label: Words in Context — Common Meaning
traps.description: Selects the word's most frequent dictionary sense rather than the sense the sentence requires.
traps.distractor_recipe: Include a word whose everyday meaning fits the topic but not the syntactic slot.
traps.tell: Choice is the word the student would have used casually.
traps.remediation_cue: Predict a replacement word before reading the options.

traps.label: Reversed Sense
traps.description: Selects a word or completion whose meaning runs opposite to the relationship the text establishes — confirming where the text disputes, increasing where it decreases.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer the clean antonym of the correct choice, phrased so it reads naturally in the sentence on its own.
traps.tell: The choice is fluent in isolation and inverts the passage's logic.
traps.remediation_cue: Predict the direction — supports or opposes, rises or falls — before reading the options.

traps.label: Evidence Matches Topic, Not Claim
traps.description: Selects data or a quotation that concerns the right subject but does not support the specific claim.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer a true reading of the table that is irrelevant to the stated hypothesis.
traps.tell: Student justifies the choice by naming the topic, not the logical link.
traps.remediation_cue: State the claim in one sentence, then ask what would have to be true.

traps.label: Rhetorical Goal Ignored
traps.description: In Rhetorical Synthesis, selects an accurate sentence that does not serve the stated rhetorical goal.
traps.distractor_recipe: Offer options that are all factually consistent with the notes; only one serves the goal.
traps.tell: All options are true; student picks on fluency.
traps.remediation_cue: Read the goal clause last and treat it as the only criterion.
